headline: 1,036 children dead as Bangladesh faces world's largest active measles outbreak
summary: Over 153,000 suspected cases have been reported, with critical gaps in vaccination coverage and contradictory government data exposing a governance failure.
details: As of September 15, Bangladesh has recorded 1,036 child deaths due to measles. According to the DGHS, 153,279 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized since mid-March.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) currently lists Bangladesh's outbreak as the largest active measles outbreak in the world.

caption:
1,036 children dead and the world's largest active measles outbreak. Why is the coverage gap still here?

As of September 15, Bangladesh has recorded 1,036 child deaths due to measles. According to the DGHS, 153,279 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized since mid-March.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) currently lists Bangladesh's outbreak as the largest active measles outbreak in the world.

An emergency vaccination drive in April targeted 1.80 crore children, but data suggests a significant gap. While a subsequent Vitamin A campaign reached 2.23 crore children, over 40 lakh children appear to have been missed by the measles vaccine.

Actual vaccination coverage is estimated to be closer to 77 percent, far below the 95 percent required for herd immunity, despite official claims of 103 percent coverage.

Hospitals are currently overwhelmed, with children being treated on floors due to a lack of beds and shortages of pediatric saline.

More than 1,000 new suspected cases are being logged every 24 hours, prompting the government to announce a 'catch-up' vaccination campaign starting later this month.

Experts call for a reconciled record of vaccinations, district-level data publication, and door-to-door outreach to prevent further undercounting and governance failures.

headline: Bangladesh tops South Asia in gender gap index, but falls 55 places globally
summary: The country ranks 79th out of 145 nations in the 2026 Global Gender Gap Index, maintaining its regional lead despite a significant drop in global ranking.
details: Bangladesh ranks 79th out of 145 countries in the Global Gender Gap Index 2026, retaining the top position in South Asia. However, its global score fell by one of the largest margins recorded this year.
The country's overall gender parity score is 71.2 percent, meaning a 28.8 percent gap remains. This is 6.2 percentage points lower than the previous edition, though still higher than its 2006 level.
Political Empowerment is the strongest area for Bangladesh, ranking 12th globally with a score of 50.9 percent. The country has maintained full parity on the head-of-state indicator since 2019.
Educational Attainment reached its highest score yet at 96.1 percent, with full parity achieved in primary and secondary school enrolment.
Health and Survival remained steady at 96 percent, with the sex ratio at birth holding steady.
Economic Participation and Opportunity is the lowest-scoring area at 41.9 percent. Parity in estimated earned income fell by 15 percentage points since the last edition.
Over the past 20 years, labour force participation parity has dropped from 61.1 percent in 2006 to 48 percent in 2026.
While women's share of ministerial posts rose to 23.5 percent, parity in Parliament remains an exception, falling to a record low of 2.4 percent in 2026.
caption:
Bangladesh remains the leader in South Asia for gender equality, but its global rank has plummeted 55 places.

Bangladesh ranks 79th out of 145 countries in the Global Gender Gap Index 2026, retaining the top position in South Asia. However, its global score fell by one of the largest margins recorded this year.

The country's overall gender parity score is 71.2 percent, meaning a 28.8 percent gap remains. This is 6.2 percentage points lower than the previous edition, though still higher than its 2006 level.

Political Empowerment is the strongest area for Bangladesh, ranking 12th globally with a score of 50.9 percent. The country has maintained full parity on the head-of-state indicator since 2019.

Educational Attainment reached its highest score yet at 96.1 percent, with full parity achieved in primary and secondary school enrolment.

Health and Survival remained steady at 96 percent, with the sex ratio at birth holding steady.

Economic Participation and Opportunity is the lowest-scoring area at 41.9 percent. Parity in estimated earned income fell by 15 percentage points since the last edition.

Over the past 20 years, labour force participation parity has dropped from 61.1 percent in 2006 to 48 percent in 2026.

While women's share of ministerial posts rose to 23.5 percent, parity in Parliament remains an exception, falling to a record low of 2.4 percent in 2026.
